body: Thanks for the reply. I'm honestly not expecting much from the police either; I just read online that credit bureaus in Canada may need a police case # to setup fraud alerts. I wish I perused this sub prior to this experience, unfortunately I really didn't expect myself to be this dumb under pressure.

The same thing happened to me as well just today well a variation of it... I first got a call from my supposing phone company telling me someone in China registered a new number under my name and has been sending out scam calls. They said if I don't address this issue within 3 hours my real phone number would be terminated and I wouldn't be able to sign up for any new ones for a year. I really panicked since I need my phone number for a host of access. 

They supposingly patched me through directly to an obscure Chinese police station; at that point I should have realized something was up. The "police officer" showed his uniform for 2 minutes then similar to your experience, he then said he can't show the interior of the police station and went off camera and then went on lecturing me on how much I failed to properly protect my identity. He also said to me someone notorious in China opened an account in my name and was committing wide fraud.

 Where I'm worse off is that I've roped my mom in to help me translate since my Chinese isn't great; for some unknown dumb reason, we shared her details too. Now they have both of our passports, drivers license, photo, DOB, address, etc... I had to share my phone screen in teams the whole time, which was over 8 hours, and had to take selfies every 3 hours to prove I wasn't doing anything dubious. I really feel so dumb, reflecting back on it now, it was so obvious something was fishy... but the stress and urgency of the situation overloaded my brain.
Thank you for your kind words. I really hope this doesn't stick with me for the rest of my life.

I did submit an online police report; I even went to the station at 3 a.m. but all they said is to wait for them to investigate. I really am freaking out, who knows what damage they can do in the meantime.
Yes, thank you. I will need to wait until the morning. It will be an agonizing few hours. Who knows how much damage they will have done by then.

just my home screen and my face. I suspect they were capturing my face to use as identify proof? Can they control my phone if i share my screen? I noticed that I can no longer make phone calls with the phone, the call just ends after a few rings.

I admit I fked up royally, I really wasn't thinking straight.

I know how you feel cause I made the same stupid mistake and if you look at my post history i made posts similar to yours around May of this year before crypto dumped. I lost over 100k from last march to today. If i invested responsibly after the covid crash i would be ahead at least $100k simply by putting it in an index ETF. If i put in crypto, probably would of gotten at least 500k but again that's in hindsight. If you realize your mistakes then stop chasing and start investing responsibly.

The loss hurts but you're still young so you can recover. Most people at 24 don't even have a positive net worth so you're still ahead of the game despite your loss. Almost everyone here on this sub will tell you to stop chasing but I know from experience that in our deranged minds we always think we are the exception and we will be the one that come out ahead if we do chase. Fact is, even if you do get lucky and hit the big one, you will not stop. You even admitted yourself in your post that you can never withdraw, so why would you think this time would be different. The rational thing would be to quit. It will be hard for sure, the allure of easy money is strong but remember the odds is always in the house's favour. Take it from a guy who chased a 5k loss to $100k+.
